narrative.overview:
AdopyHzEditor is a focused instrument bench: the audio evidence and hand-authored music data occupy the work surface, while the interface forms a quiet frame around them. Its restraint is functional rather than austere. Compact controls, stable geometry, and a near-black canvas keep repeated listening, reading, selecting, and editing comfortable during long desktop sessions.

The hierarchy is editor-first. The Canvas dominates; transport and navigation support it; the collapsible Inspector follows the current Note or Frequency Track selection; infrequent configuration stays folded under Settings. Color carries operational meaning, never decoration, and the interface avoids ornamental motion, large headings, or promotional styling.
keyCharacteristics: Canvas-dominant desktop composition with compact, persistent chrome.
Restrained charcoal surfaces separated by borders and tonal steps.
Contextual editing driven by selection, with configuration folded away.
Blue for ordinary actions and Notes, cyan for Frequency Tracks, yellow for selection, white for playback position, and gold/red for warnings and errors.
Stable, dense controls and tabular data readouts built for precision.

rules.name: The Semantic Canvas Rule
rules.body: Blue is editable Note data, cyan is analysis-derived Track evidence, yellow is current selection, and white is current playback time. Never reuse those hues decoratively on the Canvas.

rules.name: The Spectrum Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Spectrum color comes from the active analysis colormap and settings. Do not force it into a brand gradient, label its layers as melody/harmony/noise, or let chrome styling reduce its readability.

rules.name: The Instrument Readout Rule
rules.body: Values that change with playback, cursor movement, or selection use the data face and stable width; prose and control names stay in the system UI face.

rules.name: The Canvas Wins Rule
rules.body: New persistent UI must not take space from the Canvas when it can be contextual, collapsible, folded, or placed in an existing menu.

rules.name: The Stable Geometry Rule
rules.body: Playback, selection, loading, and hover updates must not resize bars, move controls, or reflow the workspace.

rules.name: The Rendering Budget Rule
rules.body: Keep Spectrum and Track work viewport-bound and generation-safe: reuse decoded/offscreen rasters and region caches, request only the visible time/pitch window at the current pixel dimensions, preserve stale-response gates and prefetch limits, and retain Track level-of-detail that favors coherent long/strong paths when zoomed out. Cursor readout reporting remains throttled, and the lightweight playback cursor remains on its separate overlay Canvas so playback does not redraw the analysis layer.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: Persistent editor regions are divided by tone and seams, not shadows. A shadow means the element floats above the work and temporarily owns interaction.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Start at 4px for controls and deviate only for a documented structural reason: 3px for tiny keys, 5px for compact containers/tabs, and 8px for modal shells.

dos: Do preserve the editor-first order: Canvas, supporting playback/navigation, contextual Inspector, then folded Settings.
Do keep ordinary controls within the established 28–32px desktop density while preserving visible focus, labels, and the 24px minimum pointer-target floor.
Do use borders, tonal layers, stable dimensions, and semantic color to communicate state.
Do keep hover information in the Canvas readout and selection-driven actions in the Inspector.
Do preserve keyboard semantics, disabled/error/empty states, wheel mappings, generation guards, selection invariants, and viewport-bound rendering.
donts: Don't add file Open/Save/Import/Export commands to the toolbar; they belong in the File menu.
Don't add dedicated ±1-second seek buttons, Note Preset UI, or a dedicated Quantize button.
Don't put Track actions back on top of the Canvas or expose every setting at once.
Don't build card-in-card layouts, decorative gradients, ornamental animation, oversized headings, or soft marketing-page spacing.
Don't use color alone for selection/status, invent musical meaning for analysis Tracks, or describe Vorbis Direct as AI transcription.
Don't let narrow-desktop compression hide core controls, cause horizontal overflow, or permanently reduce the Canvas more than the documented Inspector widths.
